What’s new

Release notes for Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management

Release notes for Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management

Learn about Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management 5.0 new features and enhancements, support, deprecations, removals, and fixed issues for errata releases.

Important: Cluster lifecycle components and features are within the multicluster engine operator, which is a software operator that enhances cluster fleet management. Release notes for multicluster engine operator-specific features are found in at Release notes for the multicluster engine operator.

Access the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management Support Matrix to learn about hub cluster and managed cluster requirements and support for each component. For lifecycle information, see Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform Life Cycle policy.

  • New features and enhancements for Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management

  • Fixed issues for Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management

  • Known issues Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management

  • Deprecations and removals for Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management

  • Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes considerations for GDPR readiness

  • FIPS readiness

Important: OpenShift Container Platform release notes are not documented in this product documentation. For your OpenShift Container Platform cluster, see OpenShift Container Platform release notes.

Best practice: Update to the most recent version.

  • If you experience issues with one of the currently supported releases, or the product documentation, go to Red Hat Support where you can troubleshoot, view Knowledgebase articles, connect with the Support Team, or open a case. You must log in with your credentials.

  • You can also learn more about the Customer Portal documentation at Red Hat Customer Portal FAQ.

New features and enhancements for Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management

New features and enhancements for Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management

Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes 5.0 provides visibility of your entire Kubernetes domain with built-in governance, cluster lifecycle management, and application lifecycle management with GitOps, along with observability.

Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management version 5.0 is released with the multicluster engine operator version 5.0 for Cluster lifecycle management. To learn about cluster management this release, see the Release notes for the multicluster engine operator.

Access the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management Support Matrix to learn about hub cluster and managed cluster requirements and support for each component. For lifecycle information, see Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform Life Cycle policy.

Learn specific details about new features for components within Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management. Important: The Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management 5.0 feature documentation, such as new or changed processes, is delayed for the release.

Installation

  • The multicluster engine operator subscription now automatically inherits the approval setting from the MultiClusterHub subscription. This allows you to configure multicluster engine operator subscription approval to manual or automatic. The manual approval setting can be configured if you do not want clusters to be automatically upgraded.

  • The multicluster engine operator discovery includes additional metadata fields to contain information from OpenShift Cluster Manager subscriptions. This metadata provides more granular control over the discovery process by improving cluster classification, support tier visibility, and environment distinction without requiring additional API calls. Additionally, the DiscoveredCluster resource contains a status field that tracks the import time and the name of the related ManagedCluster resource.

  • The new installation channel, stable-5.0, is available in this release of Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management. The release-5.0 channel continues to be supported in addition for legacy compatibility.

  • Network policy support is enhanced for the multicluster engine operator in order to deploy network policies associated with Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management components.

  • The Maestro component is deprecated and disabled in the multicluster engine operator.

Console

  • When deleting a managed cluster, you can now preserve the underlying cluster infrastructure by selecting the Preserve cluster infrastructure option in the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management console. This new option in the user interface sets the preserveOnDelete field without requiring command line access.

  • You can now preserve resources on deletion when configuring the sync policy in the console for ApplicationSet resources. Setting the preserveResourcesOnDeletion safety flag prevents accidental deletion of child Application resources when an ApplicationSet is removed or when placement changes cause applications to be pruned from spoke clusters.

  • The console now displays more specific NodePool health status updates for hosted clusters. The updated status messages include error and warning states to help operators identify issues directly from the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management console.

  • The console welcome page contains a new card describing search capabilities and a link to the external Open Cluster Management project, on the technical community card.

  • References to Red Hat Insights are rebranded to Red Hat Lightspeed in the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management console to align with updated branding across Red Hat. Updated references include user interface labels, external links, and localized text across all supported locales.

Clusters

  • You can now add rich-text descriptions to the cluster details page to help with managing large fleets. Use the Description field to annotate clusters with Markdown-formatted text and clickable links to per-cluster tools, such as monitoring dashboards, logging endpoints, and runbooks, which are displayed on the cluster overview page.

  • You can navigate more easily between clusters with usability improvements on the hub cluster and managed cluster consoles. The managed cluster list contains a link to each managed cluster console, and the console for each managed cluster contains a link to the hub cluster.

Applications and GitOps

  • The ManagedCluster registry is integrated with the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management GitOps add-on. You can now use the ManagedClusterImageRegistry resource to configure image mirroring when using the Red Hat OpenShift GitOps add-on for disconnected clusters from other Kubernetes providers.

Observability

  • You can now configure the multicluster observability add-on to automatically discover user-defined ScrapeConfig, PrometheusRule, and PrometheusAgent configurations and attach them to target placements without manually patching the ClusterManagementAddOn resource.

  • The multicluster observability add-on now supports automatic alert forwarding from managed clusters to the Alertmanager on the hub cluster.

  • The multicluster observability add-on now deploys dependent custom resource definitions from the endpoint monitoring operator on managed clusters, which reduces the impact on etcd resources on the hub cluster. This improvement is more significant in deployments with many managed clusters.

  • Perses dashboards are now generally available and fully supported. You can enable Perses dashboards to view hub cluster and managed cluster metrics from the OpenShift Container Platform console, and build real-time views of metrics, traces, logs, and profiling data from a single interface.

  • Alerts sent from managed clusters are now routed through the Observatorium API on the hub cluster, which fans out each request to all Alertmanager replicas. This ensures consistent state across all Alertmanager replicas to avoid sending duplicate alerts.

  • Technology Preview: You can now collect high-resolution metrics from managed clusters to the hub cluster more frequently than 90 seconds by configuring raw resolution on ScrapeConfig resources when using the multicluster observability add-on.

Governance

  • The Governance and Search components in Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management now use the specialized policy types used by Kyverno to ensure accurate compliance reporting and resource discovery across managed clusters, and improve performance. In Kyverno, ClusterPolicy is superseded by Common Expression Language (CEL) based policy types, including ValidatingPolicy, MutatingPolicy, GeneratingPolicy, CleanupPolicy, and ImageValidatingPolicy, which are available in this release of Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management.

Support

  • Must-gather reports now include component version information. This helps support teams and administrators to more easily identify installation-related issues without reviewing version details from individual deployment resources.

Learn more about this release

  • Get an overview of Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management from the Welcome to Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes topic.

  • See the Multicluster architecture topic to learn more about major components of the product.

Uninstalling and reinstalling earlier versions with an update can fail

Uninstalling Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management from OpenShift Container Platform can cause issues if you later want to install earlier versions and then update. For instance, when you uninstall Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management, then install an earlier version of Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management and update that version, the update might fail. The update fails if the custom resources were not removed.

Procedure

  • Follow the Cleaning up artifacts before reinstalling procedure to prevent this problem.

Additional resources

  • ACM-14343

The kubevirt-hyperconverged add-on is stuck in in progress during update

During an update from Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management 2.17 to 5.0, the kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator resource is not cleaned up and you receive the following error in the ManifestWork resource:

Failed to apply manifest: operatorpolicies.policy.open-cluster-management.io
"kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator" is forbidden: User
"system:serviceaccount:open-cluster-management-agent:klusterlet-work-sa"
cannot get resource "operatorpolicies" in API group
"policy.open-cluster-management.io" in the namespace "open-cluster-management-policies"

To resolve the issue, complete the following steps:

Procedure

  1. Remove existing resources. Run the following commands:

    oc delete clustermanagementaddon kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator --ignore-not-found

oc delete addontemplate kubevirt-hyperconverged-operator --ignore-not-found

  2. Get the namespace that is specified in the installer.namespace label of the kubevirt-hyperconverged ClusterManagementAddOn resource. Run the following command and record the output to use in step 4:

    oc get clustermanagementaddon kubevirt-hyperconverged -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.installer\.namespace}'

  3. Delete the previous ClusterManagementAddOn resource, which is version v1alpha1. Run the following command:

    oc delete clustermanagementaddon kubevirt-hyperconverged

  4. Create the ClusterManagementAddOn resource. See the following example and replace <installer_namespace> with the value that you retrieved in the previous step:

    apiVersion: addon.open-cluster-management.io/v1beta1
kind: ClusterManagementAddOn
metadata:
  name: kubevirt-hyperconverged
  annotations:
    addon.open-cluster-management.io/lifecycle: "addon-manager"
spec:
  addOnMeta:
    description: Kubevirt Hyperconverged
    displayName: Kubevirt Hyperconverged
  defaultConfigs:
    - group: addon.open-cluster-management.io
      resource: addontemplates
      name: kubevirt-hyperconverged
  installStrategy:
    type: Placements
    placements:
    - name: openshift-cnv
      namespace: <installer_namespace>

  5. Run the following command to apply your resource:

    oc apply -f <filename.yaml>

  • Passive configurations do not display managed clusters

Passive sync restore does not recover after transient BackupStorageLocation failures

When you configure a Restore resource in passive sync mode by setting syncRestoreWithNewBackups to true, and the BackupStorageLocation becomes temporarily unavailable, the Velero restore operation fails with a FailedValidation status.

After you restore the BackupStorageLocation and create successsful backups, the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management Restore resource remains in the Error phase. This happens because failed Velero restore objects persist in the cluster, which prevents the controller from attempting new restores.

The issue causes the following conditions:

  • The secondary hub cluster appears unhealthy.

  • Automated disaster recovery scripts or tools identify the cluster as not ready for switchover.

  • The Restore operation does not automatically resume sync operations after you resolve the BackupStorageLocation issue.

Procedure

  • Delete the failed Velero restore objects. Run the following command. Replace <failed_restore_name> with the name of the failed Velero restore object:

    oc -n open-cluster-management-backup delete restore.velero.io <failed_restore_name>

    After the failed objects are deleted, the Restore controller performs the following actions:

    • Detects that the Velero restore objects are missing.

    • Creates new Velero restore objects based on the latest backups.

    • Updates the Restore resource phase to Enabled.

Velero restore limitations

A new hub cluster can have a different configuration than the active hub cluster if the new hub cluster, where the data is restored, has user-created resources. For example, this can include an existing policy that was created on the new hub cluster before the backup data is restored on the new hub cluster.

Velero skips existing resources if they are not part of the restored backup, so the policy on the new hub cluster remains unchanged, resulting in a different configuration between the new hub cluster and active hub cluster.

To address this limitation, the cluster backup and restore operator runs a post restore operation to clean up the resources created by the user or a different restore operation when a restore.cluster.open-cluster-management.io resource is created. For more information, see the Post restore clean up topic.

  • ACM-1890

The appliedmanifestwork is not removed after restoring the hub cluster

When the hub cluster data is restored on the new hub cluster, the appliedmanifestwork is not removed from managed clusters that have a placement rule for an application subscription that is not a fixed cluster set.

See the following example of a placement rule for an application subscription that is not a fixed cluster set:

spec:
  clusterReplicas: 1
  clusterSelector:
    matchLabels:
      environment: dev

As a result, the application is orphaned when the managed cluster is detached from the restored hub cluster.

Procedure

  1. Specify a fixed cluster set in the placement rule. See the following example:

    spec:
  clusterSelector:
    matchLabels:
      environment: dev

  2. Delete the remaining appliedmanifestwork manually by running the following command:

    oc delete appliedmanifestwork <the-left-appliedmanifestwork-name>

Managed clusters with custom CA certificates fail to reconnect after hub restore

After you restore the backup of a hub cluster that manages a cluster with custom CA certificates, the connection between the managed cluster and the hub cluster might fail. This is because the CA certificate was not backed up on the restored hub cluster.

Procedure

  • Copy the custom CA certificate information that is in the namespace of your managed cluster to the <managed_cluster>-admin-kubeconfig secret on the restored hub cluster.

    Note: If you copy this CA certificate to the hub cluster before creating the backup copy, the backup copy includes the secret information. When you use the backup copy to restore in the future, the connection between the hub cluster and managed cluster automatically completes.

klusterlet-addon-search pod fails

The klusterlet-addon-search pod fails because the memory limit is reached.

Procedure

  • Update the memory request and limit by customizing the klusterlet-addon-search deployment on your managed cluster. Edit the ManagedclusterAddon custom resource named search-collector, on your hub cluster. Add the following annotations to the search-collector and update the memory, addon.open-cluster-management.io/search_memory_request=512Mi and addon.open-cluster-management.io/search_memory_limit=1024Mi.

    For example, if you have a managed cluster named foobar, run the following command to change the memory request to 512Mi and the memory limit to 1024Mi:

    oc annotate managedclusteraddon search-collector -n foobar \
addon.open-cluster-management.io/search_memory_request=512Mi \
addon.open-cluster-management.io/search_memory_limit=1024Mi

  • ACM-10143

Search PostgreSQL pod is in CrashLoopBackoff state

The search-postgres pod is in CrashLoopBackoff state. If Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management is deployed in a cluster with nodes that have the hugepages parameter enabled and the search-postgres pod gets scheduled in these nodes, then the pod does not start.

Complete the following steps to increase the memory of the search-postgres pod:

Procedure

  1. Pause the search-operator pod with the following command:

    oc annotate search search-v2-operator search-pause=true

  2. Update the search-postgres deployment with a limit for the hugepages parameter. Run the following command to set the hugepages parameter to 512Mi:

    oc patch deployment search-postgres --type json -p '[{"op": "add", "path": "/spec/template/spec/containers/0/resources/limits/hugepages-2Mi", "value":"512Mi"}]'

  3. Before you verify the memory usage for the pod, make sure your search-postgres pod is in the Running state. Run the following command:

    oc get pod <your-postgres-pod-name>  -o jsonpath="Status: {.status.phase}"

  4. Run the following command to verify the memory usage of the search-postgres pod:

    oc get pod <your-postgres-pod-name> -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].resources.limits.hugepages-2Mi}'

    The following value appears: 512Mi.

The local-cluster might not be automatically recreated

Local-cluster status offline after reimporting with a different name

When you accidentally try to reimport the cluster named local-cluster as a cluster with a different name, the status for local-cluster and for the reimported cluster display offline. To recover from this case, complete the following steps:

Procedure

  1. Run the following command on the hub cluster to edit the setting for self-management of the hub cluster temporarily:

    oc edit mch -n open-cluster-management multiclusterhub

  2. Add the setting spec.disableSelfManagement=true.

  3. Run the following command on the hub cluster to delete and redeploy the local-cluster:

    oc delete managedcluster local-cluster

  4. Enter the following command to remove the local-cluster management setting:

    oc edit mch -n open-cluster-management multiclusterhub

  5. Remove spec.disableSelfManagement=true that you previously added.

Subscription users without administrator rights cannot deploy cluster-scoped resources

If you don’t have the open-cluster-management:subscription-admin ClusterRoleBinding, and create or update a Subscription resource, the subscription cannot deploy cluster-scoped resources through a Git, Helm repository, or object storage channel subscription. Examples of some cluster-scoped resources include ClusterRoleBinding, ClusterRole, Namespace, and CustomResourceDefinition.

As a result, the subscription deploys only namespace-scoped resources.

Procedure

  • Bind the user who creates or updates the Subscription resource to the open-cluster-management:subscription-admin ClusterRoleBinding on the hub cluster.

Additional resources

  • ACM-39827

ManifestWork-based Pull model applications are rejected in non-default ApplicationSet namespaces

When an ApplicationSet runs outside the openshift-gitops namespace by using the ApplicationSet in any namespace feature, the controller creates generated pull-model Application objects in that custom namespace.

The tenant-isolation check requires a PlacementDecision in the Application namespace that selects the target cluster before the controller creates a ManifestWork. Without that PlacementDecision, the controller silently rejects the applications, and the applications never propagate to managed clusters.

The check prevents a namespace with only the permission to create Application resources from targeting any managed cluster.

Procedure

  • Create a ManagedClusterSetBinding and a Placement that selects the target cluster or clusters in the ApplicationSet namespace. See the following example:

    apiVersion: cluster.open-cluster-management.io/v1beta2
kind: ManagedClusterSetBinding
metadata:
  name: global
  namespace: <applicationset-namespace>
spec:
  clusterSet: global
---
apiVersion: cluster.open-cluster-management.io/v1beta1
kind: Placement
metadata:
  name: my-managed-cluster-1
  namespace: <applicationset-namespace>
spec:
  tolerations:
  - key: cluster.open-cluster-management.io/unreachable
    operator: Exists
  - key: cluster.open-cluster-management.io/unavailable
    operator: Exists
  predicates:
  - requiredClusterSelector:
      labelSelector:
        matchExpressions:
        - key: name
          operator: In
          values:
          - <target-managed-cluster-name>
Additional resources

  • ACM-39827

Cluster administrator subscriptions delay initial resource deployment

Subscriptions that use cluster-admin privilege elevation on a managed cluster experience a delay in initial resource deployment. The subscription controller confirms cluster administrator eligibility by checking whether the subscription appears in the status.appliedResources field of the AppliedManifestWork. The work agent populates the field at different times after you create the subscription.

If the first local subscription reconcile runs before the work agent updates that status, the controller treats the cluster-admin status as unresolved and does not deploy resources during that reconcile cycle. As a result, the deployment is delayed.

If the work agent status is up to date when the first reconcile runs, no delay occurs. Otherwise, resource deployment begins after one to three subscription reconcile loops complete. The default reconcile interval in appsub mode is 3 minutes for each loop, so deployment can begin up to 9 minutes after you create the subscription.

  • ACM-8889

Helm Chart with secret dependencies cannot be deployed by subscription

Using Helm Chart, you can define privacy data in a Kubernetes secret and refer to this secret within the value.yaml file of the Helm Chart.

The username and password are given by the referred Kubernetes secret resource dbsecret. For example, see the following sample value.yaml file:

credentials:
  secretName: dbsecret
  usernameSecretKey: username
  passwordSecretKey: password

The Helm Chart with secret dependencies is only supported in the Helm binary CLI. It is not supported in the operator SDK Helm library. The Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management subscription controller applies the operator SDK Helm library to install and upgrade the Helm Chart. Therefore, the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management subscription cannot deploy the Helm Chart with secret dependencies.

  • ACM-6954

Local cluster is excluded as a managed cluster for pull model

The hub cluster application set deploys to target managed clusters, but the local cluster, which is a managed hub cluster, is excluded as a target managed cluster.

As a result, if the Argo CD application is propagated to the local cluster by the Argo CD pull model, the local cluster Argo CD application is not cleaned up, even though the local cluster is removed from the placement decision of the Argo CD ApplicationSet resource.

Additionally, if you manually refresh the pull model Argo CD application in the Applications section of the Argo CD console, the refresh is not processed and the REFRESH button in the Argo CD console is disabled.

Procedure

  1. Remove the skip-reconcile annotation from the local cluster Argo CD application. See the following annotation:

    annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/skip-reconcile: "true"

  2. Remove the refresh annotation from the Argo CD application. See the following annotation:

    annotations:
    argocd.argoproj.io/refresh: normal

  • ACM-7843

Argo CD and propagation controllers might reconcile simultaneously

Both the Argo CD controller and the propagation controller might reconcile on the same application resource and cause the duplicate instances of application deployment on the managed clusters, but from the different deployment models.

For deploying applications by using the pull model, the Argo CD controllers ignore these application resources when the Argo CD argocd.argoproj.io/skip-reconcile annotation is added to the template section of the ApplicationSet.

The argocd.argoproj.io/skip-reconcile annotation is only available in the GitOps operator version 1.9.0, or later.

Procedure

  • Wait until the hub cluster and all the managed clusters are updated to GitOps operator version 1.9.0 before implementing the pull model.

Resource fails to deploy

All the resources listed in the MulticlusterApplicationSetReport are actually deployed on the managed clusters. If a resource fails to deploy, the resource is not included in the resource list, but the cause is listed in the error message.

Resource allocation might take several minutes

For large environments with over 1000 managed clusters and Argo CD application sets that are deployed to hundreds of managed clusters, Argo CD application creation on the hub cluster might take several minutes.

Procedure

  • Set the requeueAfterSeconds to zero in the clusterDecisionResource generator of the application set, as it is displayed in the following example file:

    apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: ApplicationSet
metadata:
  name: cm-allclusters-app-set
  namespace: openshift-gitops
spec:
  generators:
  - clusterDecisionResource:
      configMapRef: ocm-placement-generator
      labelSelector:
        matchLabels:
          cluster.open-cluster-management.io/placement: app-placement
      requeueAfterSeconds: 0
Application ObjectBucket channel type cannot use allow and deny lists

You cannot specify allow and deny lists with ObjectBucket channel type in the subscription-admin role. In other channel types, the allow and deny lists in the subscription indicates which Kubernetes resources can be deployed, and which Kubernetes resources should not be deployed.

Additional resources

  • GH-22763

Changes to the multicluster_operators_subscription image do not take effect automatically

The application-manager add-on that is running on the managed clusters is now handled by the subscription operator, when it was previously handled by the klusterlet operator. The subscription operator is not managed the multicluster-hub, so changes to the multicluster_operators_subscription image in the multicluster-hub image manifest config map do not take effect automatically.

If the image that is used by the subscription operator is overrided by changing the multicluster_operators_subscription image in the multicluster-hub image manifest config map, the application-manager add-on on the managed clusters does not use the new image until the subscription operator pod is restarted.

Policy resource not deployed unless by subscription administrator

The policy.open-cluster-management.io/v1 resources are no longer deployed by an application subscription by default for Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management version 2.4. policy.open-cluster-management.io/v1 resources that were deployed by existing application subscriptions in previous Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management versions remain, but are no longer reconciled with the source repository unless the application subscriptions are deployed by a subscription administrator.

Procedure

  • Deploy the application subscription as a subscription administrator. See Create an allow and deny list as subscription administrator for information.

Additional resources

  • ACM-893

Application Ansible hook stand-alone mode

Ansible hook stand-alone mode is not supported. To deploy Ansible hook on the hub cluster with a subscription, you might use the following subscription YAML:

apiVersion: apps.open-cluster-management.io/v1
kind: Subscription
metadata:
  name: sub-rhacm-gitops-demo
  namespace: hello-openshift
  annotations:
    apps.open-cluster-management.io/github-path: myapp
    apps.open-cluster-management.io/github-branch: master
spec:
  hooksecretref:
      name: toweraccess
  channel: rhacm-gitops-demo/ch-rhacm-gitops-demo
  placement:
     local: true

However, this configuration might never create the Ansible instance, since the spec.placement.local:true has the subscription running on standalone mode. You need to create the subscription in hub mode.

Procedure

  1. Create a placement rule that deploys to local-cluster. See the following sample where local-cluster: "true" refers to your hub cluster:

    apiVersion: apps.open-cluster-management.io/v1
kind: PlacementRule
metadata:
  name: <towhichcluster>
  namespace: hello-openshift
spec:
  clusterSelector:
    matchLabels:
      local-cluster: "true"

  2. Reference that placement rule in your subscription. See the following sample:

    apiVersion: apps.open-cluster-management.io/v1
kind: Subscription
metadata:
  name: sub-rhacm-gitops-demo
  namespace: hello-openshift
  annotations:
    apps.open-cluster-management.io/github-path: myapp
    apps.open-cluster-management.io/github-branch: master
spec:
  hooksecretref:
      name: toweraccess
  channel: rhacm-gitops-demo/ch-rhacm-gitops-demo
  placement:
     placementRef:
        name: <towhichcluster>
        kind: PlacementRule

    After applying both, you should see the Ansible instance created in your hub cluster.

Additional resources

  • GH-8036

Application not deployed after an updated placement rule

If applications are not deploying after an update to a placement rule, verify that the application-manager pod is running. The application-manager is the subscription container that needs to run on managed clusters.

Procedure

  1. Run the following command to verify that the application-manager is running:

    oc get pods -n open-cluster-management-agent-addon |grep application-manager

  2. Search for kind:pod cluster:yourcluster in the console and see if the application-manager is running.

  3. If you cannot verify, attempt to import the cluster again and verify again.

Subscription operator does not create an SCC

Learn about Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform SCC at Managing security context constraints, which is an additional configuration required on the managed cluster.

Different deployments have different security context and different service accounts. The subscription operator cannot create an SCC CR automatically.. Administrators control permissions for pods. A Security Context Constraints (SCC) CR is required to enable appropriate permissions for the relative service accounts to create pods in the non-default namespace. To manually create an SCC CR in your namespace, complete the following steps:

Procedure

  1. Find the service account that is defined in the deployments. For example, see the following nginx deployments:

    nginx-ingress-52edb
nginx-ingress-52edb-backend

  2. Create an SCC CR in your namespace to assign the required permissions to the service account or accounts. See the following example, where kind: SecurityContextConstraints is added:

    apiVersion: security.openshift.io/v1
 defaultAddCapabilities:
 kind: SecurityContextConstraints
 metadata:
   name: ingress-nginx
   namespace: ns-sub-1
 priority: null
 readOnlyRootFilesystem: false
 requiredDropCapabilities:
 fsGroup:
   type: RunAsAny
 runAsUser:
   type: RunAsAny
 seLinuxContext:
   type: RunAsAny
 users:
 - system:serviceaccount:my-operator:nginx-ingress-52edb
 - system:serviceaccount:my-operator:nginx-ingress-52edb-backend

Application channels require unique namespaces

Creating more than one channel in the same namespace can cause errors with the hub cluster.

For instance, namespace charts-v1 is used by the installer as a Helm type channel, so do not create any additional channels in charts-v1.

Procedure

  • Create your channel in a unique namespace. All channels need an individual namespace, except GitHub channels, which can share a namespace with another GitHub channel.

Ansible Automation Platform job fail

Ansible jobs fail to run when you select an incompatible option. Ansible Automation Platform only works when the -cluster-scoped channel options are chosen. This affects all components that need to perform Ansible jobs.

Application console table limitations

See the following limitations to various Application tables in the console:

  • From the Applications table on the Overview page and the Subscriptions table on the Advanced configuration page, the Clusters column displays a count of clusters where application resources are deployed. Since applications are defined by resources on the local cluster, the local cluster is included in the search results, whether actual application resources are deployed on the local cluster or not.

  • From the Advanced configuration table for Subscriptions, the Applications column displays the total number of applications that use that subscription, but if the subscription deploys child applications, those are included in the search result, as well.

  • From the Advanced configuration table for Channels, the Subscriptions column displays the total number of subscriptions on the local cluster that use that channel, but this does not include subscriptions that are deployed by other subscriptions, which are included in the search result.

ClusterPermission resource fails when creating many role bindings

If you create a ClusterPermission resource that contains many role bindings within the same namespace and do not set the optional name field, it fails. This error occurs because the same name is used for the role bindings in the namespace.

Procedure

Observability known issues

Review the known issues for Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes. The following list contains known issues for this release, or known issues that continued from the previous release.

For your Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform cluster, see OpenShift Container Platform known issues.

For more about deprecations and removals, see Deprecations and removals for Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management.

  • Manually configured alert forwarding fails

  • Manually configured alert forwarding fails after upgrade

  • Retention change causes data loss

  • Observatorium API gateway pods have stale tenant data after hub restore

  • No permission to add PrometheusRules and ServiceMonitors in openshift-monitoring namespace

Manually configured alert forwarding fails

When you update to Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management 2.17 and later, alert forwarding fails if you disabled automatic configuration by setting mco-disable-alerting: true in the MultiClusterObservability custom resource, and if you manually configured alert forwarding.

Alert forwarding fails after you update because the name of the observability-alertmanager-accessor and hub-alertmanager-router-ca secrets were changed to include a postfix of the hub cluster ID.

The hub cluster ID is obtained from the uuid field in the metadata of the ClusterVersion custom resource on the hub cluster. The ID, with dashes removed and trimmed to the first 19 characters, is appended to the alertmanager secrets.

Procedure

  1. Update your alert forwarding configuration that you manually configured to use the new names of the secrets.

  2. Update the secret name in the cluster-monitoring-config config map in the openshift-monitoring namespace for platform alerts.

  3. Update the secret name in the user-workload-monitoring-config config map in the openshift-user-workload-monitoring namespace for user workload alerts.

  4. Find the new secret names in the openshift-monitoring and openshift-user-workload-monitoring namespaces.

Additional resources

  • ACM-26604

Retention change causes data loss

The default retention for all resolution levels, such as retentionResolutionRaw, retentionResolution5m, or retentionResolution1h, is 365 days (365d). This 365d default retention means that the default retention for a 1 hour resolution has decreased from indefinite, 0d to 365d. This retention change might cause you to lose data. If you did not set an explicit value for the resolution retention in your MultiClusterObservability spec.advanced.retentionConfig parameter, you might lose data. For more information, see Observability advanced configuration.

Additional resources

  • Observability advanced configuration

  • ACM-11048

Observatorium API gateway pods have stale tenant data after hub restore

The Observatorium API gateway pods in a restored hub cluster might contain stale tenant data after a backup and restore procedure because of a Kubernetes limitation. See Mounted config maps are updated automatically for more about the limitation.

As a result, the Observatorium API and Thanos gateway rejects metrics from collectors, and the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management Grafana dashboards do not display data.

See the following errors from the Observatorium API gateway pod logs:

level=error name=observatorium caller=logchannel.go:129 msg="failed to forward metrics" returncode="500 Internal Server Error" response="no matching hashring to handle tenant\n"

Thanos receives pods logs with the following errors:

caller=handler.go:551 level=error component=receive component=receive-handler tenant=xxxx err="no matching hashring to handle tenant" msg="internal server error"

See the following procedure to restart all Observatorium API gateway pods with the correct tenant information, and the data from collectors start displaying in Grafana in between 5-10 minutes:

Procedure

  1. Scale down the observability-observatorium-api deployment instances from N to 0.

  2. Scale up the observability-observatorium-api deployment instances from 0 to N.

    Note: N = 2 by default, but might be greater than 2 in some custom configuration environments.

Additional resources

  • ACM-9681

No permission to add PrometheusRules and ServiceMonitors in openshift-monitoring namespace

When Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management is deployed or an installation is updated, the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management observability ServiceMonitors and PrometheusRule resources are no longer present in the openshift-monitoring namespace.

Procedure

  • Use a label in your defined Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management hub cluster namespace. The label, openshift.io/cluster-monitoring: "true" causes the Cluster Monitoring Operator to scrape the namespace for metrics.

Additional resources

  • ACM-8499

Lack of support for proxy settings

The Prometheus AdditionalAlertManagerConfig resource of the observability add-on does not support proxy settings. You must disable the observability alert forwarding feature. Complete the following steps to disable alert forwarding:

Procedure

  1. Go to the MultiClusterObservability resource.

  2. Update the mco-disabling-alerting parameter value to true

    The HTTPS proxy with a self-signed CA certificate is not supported.

Additional resources

  • ACM-7118

Grafana downsampled data mismatch

When you attempt to query historical data and there is a discrepancy between the calculated step value and downsampled data, the result is empty. For example, if the calculated step value is 5m and the downsampled data is in a one-hour interval, data does not appear from Grafana.

This discrepancy occurs because a URL query parameter must be passed through the Thanos Query front-end data source. Afterwards, the URL query can perform additional queries for other downsampling levels when data is missing. You must manually update the Thanos Query front-end data source configuration.

Procedure

  1. Go to the Query front-end data source.

  2. To update your query parameters, click the Misc section.

  3. From the Custom query parameters field, select max_source_resolution=auto.

  4. To verify that the data is displayed, refresh your Grafana page.

    Your query data appears from the Grafana dashboard.

Additional resources

  • ACM-3748

Limitations for custom managed cluster Observatorium API or Alertmanager URLs

Custom Observatorium API and Alertmanager URLs only support intermediate components with TLS passthrough.

Procedure

  • Use separate sub-domains if both custom URLs are pointing to the same intermediate component because OpenShift Container Platform routers do not support two separate route objects with the same host.

Configuration policy listed compliant when namespace is stuck in Terminating state

When you have a configuration policy that is configured with mustnothave for the complianceType parameter and enforce for the remediationAction parameter, the policy is listed as compliant when a deletion request is made to the Kubernetes API. Therefore, the Kubernetes object can be stuck in a Terminating state while the policy is listed as compliant.

Additional resources

  • GH-20715

ConfigurationPolicy stuck in terminating

When you remove the config-policy-controller add-on from a managed cluster by disabling the policy controller in the KlusterletAddonConfig or by detaching the cluster, the ConfigurationPolicy custom resource definition might get stuck in a terminating state. If the ConfigurationPolicy custom resource definition is stuck in a terminating state, new policies might not be added to the cluster if the add-on is reinstalled later. You can also receive the following error:

template-error; Failed to create policy template: create not allowed while custom resource definition is terminating
Procedure

  1. Use the following command to check if the custom resource definition is stuck:

    oc get crd configurationpolicies.policy.open-cluster-management.io -o=jsonpath='{.metadata.deletionTimestamp}'

  2. If a deletion timestamp is on the resource, the custom resource definition is stuck. To resolve the issue, remove all finalizers from configuration policies that remain on the cluster. Use the following command on the managed cluster and replace <cluster-namespace> with the managed cluster namespace:

    oc get configurationpolicy -n <cluster-namespace> -o name | xargs oc patch -n <cluster-namespace> --type=merge -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers": []}}'

    The configuration policy resources are automatically removed from the cluster and the custom resource definition exits its terminating state. If the add-on has already been reinstalled, the custom resource definition is recreated automatically without a deletion timestamp.

Additional resources

  • GH-25139

Policy status shows repeated updates when enforced

If a policy is set to remediationAction: enforce and is repeatedly updated, the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management console shows repeated violations with successful updates. Repeated updates produce multiple policy events, which can cause the governance-policy-framework-addon pod to run out of memory and crash.

Procedure

  1. Disable the policy and compare the differences between objectDefinition in the policy and the object on the managed cluster if another controller or process is also updating the object with different values.

    If the values are different, another controller or process might be updating them. Check the metadata of the object to help identify why the values are different.

  2. Disable the policy and compare the differences between objectDefinition in the policy and the object on the managed cluster if the objectDefinition in the ConfigurationPolicy does not match because of Kubernetes processing the object when the policy is applied.

    If the keys are different or missing, Kubernetes might have processed the keys before applying them to the object, such as removing keys containing default or empty values.

The cause is that the PolicyReport API version is incorrect in the generator and does not match what Kyverno has deployed.

  • ACM-27270

Source IP not retained for applications on OpenShift Container Platform with OVN-Kubernetes

If you are using OpenShift Container Platform versions between 4.18 and versions earlier than 4.19.5 with OVN-Kubernetes for Submariner, the source IP is not retained when packets reach the destination pod. As a result, applications that rely on the source IP, such as NetworkPolicy, might not work correctly.

Additional resources

  • ACM-18680

Without ClusterManagementAddon submariner add-on fails

For versions 2.8 and earlier, when you install Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management, you also deploy the submariner-addon component with the Operator Lifecycle Manager. If you did not create a MultiClusterHub custom resource, the submariner-addon pod sends an error and prevents the operator from installing.

The following notification occurs because the ClusterManagementAddon custom resource definition is missing:

graceful termination failed, controllers failed with error: the server could not find the requested resource (post clustermanagementaddons.addon.open-cluster-management.io)

The ClusterManagementAddon resource is created by the cluster-manager deployment, however, this deployment becomes available when the MultiClusterEngine components are installed on the cluster.

If there is not a MultiClusterEngine resource that is already available on the cluster when the MultiClusterHub custom resource is created, the MultiClusterHub operator deploys the MultiClusterEngine instance and the operator that is required, which resolves the previous error.

  • GH-24159

Submariner add-on resources not cleaned up properly when managed clusters are imported

If the submariner-addon component is set to false within MultiClusterHub (MCH) operator, then the submariner-addon finalizers are not cleaned up properly for the managed cluster resources. Since the finalizers are not cleaned up properly, this prevents the submariner-addon component from being disabled within the hub cluster.

Submariner install plan limitation

The Submariner install plan does not follow the overall install plan settings. Therefore, the operator management screen cannot control the Submariner install plan. By default, Submariner install plans are applied automatically, and the Submariner add-on is always updated to the latest available version corresponding to the installed Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management version.

  • Use a customized Submariner subscription.

Deprecations and removals for Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management

Learn when parts of the product are deprecated or removed from Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes. Consider the alternative actions in the Recommended action and details, which display in the tables for the current release and for two prior releases. Best practice: Update to the most recent version.

Deprecated: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management 2.12 and earlier versions are no longer supported. The documentation might remain available, but without any errata releases for fixed issues or other updates. For lifecycle information, see Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform Life Cycle policy and Platform-aligned operators.

Important: Cluster lifecycle components and features are within the multicluster engine operator, which is a software operator that enhances cluster fleet management. Release notes for multicluster engine operator-specific features are found in at Release notes for the multicluster engine operator.

New features and enhancements for the multicluster engine operator

New features and enhancements for the multicluster engine operator

Learn about multicluster engine for Kubernetes operator 5.0 new features and enhancements, support, deprecations, removals, and fixed issues for errata releases. multicluster engine operator version 5.0 is released with Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management version 5.0 for Cluster lifecycle management, but you can use stand-alone multicluster engine operator with your OpenShift Container Platform hub cluster, as well.

For full support information, including supported OpenShift Container Platform versions, see the multicluster engine operator Support Matrix. For lifecycle information, see Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform Life Cycle policy.

Use multicluster engine operator features for creating, importing, managing, and destroying Kubernetes clusters across various infrastructure cloud providers, private clouds, and on-premises data centers.

If you are using multicluster engine operator with Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management installed afterwards, see the New features and enhancements for Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management this release.

Important:

  • Cluster management supports all providers that are certified through the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Kubernetes Conformance Program. Choose a vendor that is recognized by CNCF for your hybrid cloud multicluster management. See the following information about using CNCF providers:

  • Learn how CNCF providers are certified at Certified Kubernetes Conformance.

  • For Red Hat support information about CNCF third-party providers, see Red Hat support with third party components, or Contact Red Hat support.

  • If you bring your own CNCF conformance certified cluster, you need to change the OpenShift Container Platform CLI oc command to the Kubernetes CLI command, kubectl.

  • Some features and components are identified and released as Technology Preview.

  • New features and enhancements for multicluster engine operator 5.0 include the following changes:

    • You can now add rich-text descriptions to the cluster details page to help with managing large fleets. Use the Description field to annotate clusters with Markdown-formatted text and clickable links to per-cluster tools, such as monitoring dashboards, logging endpoints, and runbooks, which are displayed on the cluster overview page.

    • You can navigate more easily between clusters with usability improvements on the hub cluster and managed cluster consoles. The managed cluster list contains a link to each managed cluster console, and the console for each managed cluster contains a link to the hub cluster.

HyperShift not supported on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 with certain feature gates

You cannot use enable the hosted control plane feature on OpenShift Container Platform version 4.22 clusters that run on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10 if the TechPreviewNoUpgrade feature gate is enabled. If you attempt to enable hosted control plane on these clusters, the clusters become unstable.

Additional resources

  • ACM-34084

Unclaimed Hive clusters recreated during ClusterPool custom resource definition changes

During a multicluster engine operator upgrade or modification to the ClusterPool custom resource definition, Hive might delete and re-create all unclaimed clusters. This is expected behavior and ensures that unclaimed clusters reflect the latest configuration defined in the updated ClusterPool resource specification.

Additional resources

  • ACM-21686

installNamespace field can only have one value

Note: The spec.installNamespace field is deprecated. When enabling the managed-serviceaccount add-on, the installNamespace field in the ManagedClusterAddOn resource must have open-cluster-management-agent-addon as the value. Other values are ignored. The managed-serviceaccount add-on agent is always deployed in the open-cluster-management-agent-addon namespace on the managed cluster.

Additional resources

  • ACM-7523

Cluster API Provider Metal3 certificate generation fails after upgrade

After you upgrade from multicluster engine for Kubernetes operator version 2.10 or 2.10.1 to version 2.11, the automatic generation of certificates for the Cluster API Provider Metal3 webhooks fail due to a naming conflict in the target resources. As a result, webhooks do not validate.

To resolve the issue, manually delete the existing secret and the renamed service. The operator then regenerates the correct secret. Complete the following steps on your managed cluster:

Procedure

  1. Delete the webhook service. Run the following command:

    oc delete service capm3-webhook-service -n multicluster-engine

  2. Delete the Transport Layer Security (TLS) secret. Run the following command:

    oc delete secret capm3-webhook-service-cert -n multicluster-engine

  3. Clear the error annotations. Run the following command:

    oc annotate service mce-capm3-webhook-service -n multicluster-engine \
service.alpha.openshift.io/serving-cert-generation-error- \
service.alpha.openshift.io/serving-cert-generation-error-num- \
service.beta.openshift.io/serving-cert-generation-error- \
service.beta.openshift.io/serving-cert-generation-error-num-

  4. Delete the stale webhook configurations. Run the following commands:

    oc delete mutatingwebhookconfiguration capm3-mutating-webhook-configuration
    oc delete validatingwebhookconfiguration capm3-validating-webhook-configuration

  5. Delete the new TLS secret. Run the following command:

    oc delete secret mce-capm3-webhook-service-cert -n multicluster-engine

  6. Restart the pod to regenerate the certificate. Run the following command:

    oc delete pod mce-capm3-controller-manager-<hash> -n multicluster-engine

  7. Delete the old controller-manager deployment. Run the following command:

    oc delete deployment capm3-controller-manager -n multicluster-engine
Additional resources

  • MGMT-23257

Cluster API and Cluster API Provider for Azure deployments not creating pods

When you deploy cluster-api and cluster-api-provider-azure components, the Cluster API controllers might not create pods. To work around the issue, complete the following steps:

Procedure

  1. Verify that the cluster-api component is enabled. Run the following command:

    oc get mce multiclusterengine -o json | \
  jq -r '.spec.overrides.components[] | select(.name | contains("cluster-api"))'

  2. Check if the hypershift component is causing a conflict. Run the following command to check if the READY status is 0/1:

    oc get deployment -n hypershift

  3. If the status is 0/1, force multicluster engine operator reconciliation. Run the following command:

    oc annotate mce multiclusterengine force-reconcile=$(date +%s) --overwrite
Additional resources

  • ACM-30244

HyperShift conflict when creating Azure Red Hat OpenShift hosted control plane clusters with Cluster API Provider for Azure

You might not be able to create Azure Red Hat OpenShift hosted control plane clusters by using Cluster API Provider for Azure if the hypershift and cluster-api controllers are running at the same time. To resolve the issue, complete the following steps:

Procedure

  1. Disable the hypershift component. Run the following command:

    oc patch mce multiclusterengine --type=merge -p "{\"spec\":{\"overrides\":{\"components\":$(oc get mce multiclusterengine -o json | jq -c '.spec.overrides.components | map(if .name == "hypershift" then .enabled = false else . end)')}}}"

  2. Disable the hypershift-local-hosting component. Run the following command:

    oc patch mce multiclusterengine --type=merge -p "{\"spec\":{\"overrides\":{\"components\":$(oc get mce multiclusterengine -o json | jq -c '.spec.overrides.components | map(if .name == "hypershift-local-hosting" then .enabled = false else . end)')}}}"

  • ACM-30244

Microsoft Azure authentication fails when creating Azure Red Hat OpenShift hosted control plane clusters with Cluster API Provider for Azure

When you create Azure Red Hat OpenShift hosted control plane clusters by using Cluster API Provider for Azure, the cluster creation might fail because of Microsoft Azure authentication errors. To work around the issue, ensure you are connected to Microsoft Azure with your credentials. Complete the following steps:

Procedure

  1. Verify your Microsoft Azure credentials secret. Run the following command. Replace <cluster-namespace> with the namespace of your cluster:

    oc get secret aso-credential -n <cluster-namespace> -o yaml

  2. Test the Microsoft Azure connection. Run the following command:

    oc run azure-cli --rm -it --image=mcr.microsoft.com/azure-cli -- bash

  3. Log in to Microsoft Azure inside the pod. Run the following command. Replace <client_id>, <client_secret>, and <tenant_id> with your Microsoft Azure credentials:

    az login --service-principal --username <client_id> --password <client_secret> --tenant <tenant_id>
Additional resources

  • ACM-30244

Resource deletion during cluster distribution updates

When a change occurs in the cluster because of the Placement resource, cluster redistribution occurs across multiple PlacementDecisions resources. During the sequential update, a cluster is temporarily missing from all PlacementDecisions resources. Controllers that monitor PlacementDecisions resources identify this temporary deletion as cluster removal. This sequence leads to unnecessary resource deletion and recreation. For example, the addon-management-controller deletes and re-creates ManagedClusterAddOns, which cause workload disruption.

Additional resources

  • ACM-27799

HyperShift operator and Cluster API components conflict

Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management and multicluster engine operator enable the hypershift and hypershift-local-hosting components by default, which can conflict with the cluster-api and cluster-api-provider-aws components. When you enable and then disable the cluster-api and cluster-api-provider-aws components, custom resource definitions of a higher version might remain in the cluster. Manually remove the custom resource definitions before you re-enable the hypershift-local-hosting component. To manage Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (classic) clusters by using the cluster-api and cluster-api-provider-aws components, you must disable the hypershift and hypershift-local-hosting components to prevent API conflicts.

Procedure

  1. Run the following command to remove the custom resource definitions:

    oc delete crd <crd-name>

  2. Remove the following custom resource definitions:

    • clusterresourcesetbindings.addons.cluster.x-k8s.io

    • clusterresourcesets.addons.cluster.x-k8s.io

    • clusters.cluster.x-k8s.io

    • clusterclasses.cluster.x-k8s.io

    • machines.cluster.x-k8s.io

    • machinesets.cluster.x-k8s.io

    • machinedeployments.cluster.x-k8s.io

    • machinepools.cluster.x-k8s.io

    • machinehealthchecks.cluster.x-k8s.io

    • machinedrainrules.cluster.x-k8s.io

HyperShift operator does not receive infrastructure node configuration

When Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management or multicluster engine operator is installed with infrastructure node selection configured, by using nodeSelector and tolerations for infrastructure node, the HyperShift operator deployment does not receive the settings.

Even if the multicluster engine subscription is configured to place pods on infrastructure nodes by using nodeSelector and tolerations, the HyperShift operator pods are scheduled on regular worker nodes instead of the designated infrastructure nodes.

The HyperShift operator deployment does not automatically propagate the infrastructure node placement configuration from the subscription.

Procedure

  1. After you install the HyperShift add-on, manually patch the HyperShift operator deployment to add the infrastructure node selector and tolerations.

  2. Apply a patch to the operator deployment in the hypershift namespace by running the following command with the specifications for your infrastructure nodes. The manual patch ensures that the operator pods are placed on the correct nodes to comply with your infrastructure requirements.

    oc patch deployment operator -n hypershift --type=merge -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"nodeSelector":{"node-role.kubernetes.io/infra":""},"tolerations":[{"key":"node-role.kubernetes.io/infra","operator":"Exists","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'

    See the following example of a patch that adds the infrastructure node selector and tolerations to the HyperShift operator deployment:

          nodeSelector:
        node-role.kubernetes.io/infra: ""
      tolerations:
      - key: node-role.kubernetes.io/infra
        operator: Exists
        effect: NoSchedule
Additional resources

  • ACM-24191

HyperShift installation fails on Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (classic) due to admission webhook error

When you install multicluster engine for Kubernetes operator 2.10 on Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (classic), the HyperShift installation job might fail repeatedly with an admission webhook error similar to the following message: namespace-validation.managed.openshift.io denied the request. See the following explanations for the error. To resolve this issue, create a ConfigMap in the local-cluster namespace to disable platform monitoring.

  • The installation process attempts to create a hypershift namespace that includes the openshift.io/cluster-monitoring: "true" label.

  • The Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (classic) managed admission webhooks prevent users from modifying protected labels on namespaces, including the cluster-monitoring label.

  • The platform monitoring flag defaults to monitoring the operator, which adds the cluster-monitoring label to the hypershift namespace.

  • In managed environments, such as Red Hat OpenShift Service on AWS (classic), the service provider typically handles platform-level monitoring. Therefore, this monitoring is not required and conflicts with namespace protection policies.

Procedure

  1. Create a YAML file for the ConfigMap with the following content:

    kind: ConfigMap
apiVersion: v1
metadata:
  name: hypershift-operator-install-flags
  namespace: local-cluster
data:
  installFlagsToAdd: "--platform-monitoring=None"
  installFlagsToRemove: ""

  2. Apply the ConfigMap to your cluster to instruct the HyperShift installer to skip the cluster-monitoring label, which avoids the admission webhook conflict. Run the following command. Replace <filename> with the name of your YAML file:

    oc apply -f <filename>.yaml

ClusterClaim error

If you create a Hive ClusterClaim against a ClusterPool and manually set the ClusterClaimspec lifetime field to an invalid golang time value, the product stops fulfilling and reconciling all ClusterClaims, not just the malformed claim.

You see the following error in the clusterclaim-controller pod logs, which is a specific example with the PoolName and invalid lifetime included:

+

E0203 07:10:38.266841       1 reflector.go:138] sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/cache/internal/informers_map.go:224: Failed to watch *v1.ClusterClaim: failed to list *v1.ClusterClaim: v1.ClusterClaimList.Items: []v1.ClusterClaim: v1.ClusterClaim.v1.ClusterClaim.Spec: v1.ClusterClaimSpec.Lifetime: unmarshalerDecoder: time: unknown unit "w" in duration "1w", error found in #10 byte of ...|time":"1w"}},{"apiVe|..., bigger context ...|clusterPoolName":"policy-aas-hubs","lifetime":"1w"}},{"apiVersion":"hive.openshift.io/v1","kind":"Cl|...
Procedure

  • Delete the invalid claim. If the malformed claim is deleted, claims begin successfully reconciling again without any further interaction.

Additional resources

  • GH-3706

Process to destroy a cluster does not complete

When you destroy a managed cluster, the status continues to display Destroying after one hour, and the cluster is not destroyed. To resolve this issue, complete the following steps:

Procedure

  1. Manually ensure that there are no orphaned resources on your cloud, and that all of the provider resources that are associated with the managed cluster are cleaned up.

  2. Open the ClusterDeployment information for the managed cluster that is being removed by entering the following command:

    oc edit clusterdeployment/<mycluster> -n <namespace>

    • Replace mycluster with the name of the managed cluster that you are destroying.

    • Replace namespace with the namespace of the managed cluster.

  3. Remove the hive.openshift.io/deprovision finalizer to forcefully stop the process that is trying to clean up the cluster resources in the cloud.

  4. Save your changes and verify that ClusterDeployment is gone.

  5. Manually remove the namespace of the managed cluster by running the following command:

    oc delete ns <namespace>

    • Replace namespace with the namespace of the managed cluster.

Non-OpenShift Container Platform managed clusters require ManagedServiceAccount or LoadBalancer for pod logs

The ManagedServiceAccount and cluster proxy add-ons are enabled by default in Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management version 2.10 and newer. If the add-ons are disabled after upgrading, you must enable the ManagedServiceAccount and cluster proxy add-ons manually to use the pod log feature.

Additional resources

  • ACM-11034

Client cannot reach iPXE script

iPXE is an open source network boot firmware. See iPXE for more details.

When booting a node, the URL length limitation in some DHCP servers cuts off the ipxeScript URL in the InfraEnv custom resource definition, resulting in the following error message in the console:

no bootable devices

To work around the issue, complete the following steps:

Procedure

  1. Apply the InfraEnv custom resource definition when using an assisted installation to expose the bootArtifacts, which might resemble the following file:

    status:
  agentLabelSelector:
    matchLabels:
      infraenvs.agent-install.openshift.io: qe2
  bootArtifacts:
    initrd: https://assisted-image-service-multicluster-engine.redhat.com/images/0000/pxe-initrd?api_key=0000000&arch=x86_64&version=4.11
    ipxeScript: https://assisted-service-multicluster-engine.redhat.com/api/assisted-install/v2/infra-envs/00000/downloads/files?api_key=000000000&file_name=ipxe-script
    kernel: https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/dependencies/rhcos/4.12/latest/rhcos-live-kernel-x86_64
    rootfs: https://mirror.openshift.com/pub/openshift-v4/x86_64/dependencies/rhcos/4.12/latest/rhcos-live-rootfs.x86_64.img

  2. Create a proxy server to expose the bootArtifacts with short URLs.

  3. Copy the bootArtifacts and add them to the proxy by running the following commands:

    for artifact in oc get infraenv qe2 -ojsonpath="{.status.bootArtifacts}" | jq ". | keys[]" | sed "s/\"//g"
do curl -k oc get infraenv qe2 -ojsonpath="{.status.bootArtifacts.${artifact}}"` -o $artifact

  4. Add the ipxeScript artifact proxy URL to the bootp parameter in libvirt.xml.

To learn more about how to use the addonDeploymentConfig custom resource to configure tolerations and nodeSelector for add-on, see Set up the AddOnDeploymentConfig to configure klusterlet add-ons.

  • ACM-7523

Assisted Installer pulls incorrect cached image in disconnected environments

In a disconnected environment, Assisted Installer might pull an incorrect cached release image instead of the image from your disconnected registry. To work around the issue, prevent the cluster-image-set-controller from recreating the ClusterImageSet resources during deletion and delete the ClusterImageSet resources on the hub cluster to clear the hub cluster image cache. After you restart the installation, the image is pulled correctly from the disconnected registry.

Procedure

  1. Create a ConfigMap that points the controller to a Git repository that does not exist. Run the following command:

    oc create configmap cluster-image-set-git-repo -n multicluster-engine \
  --from-literal=gitRepoUrl=https://github.com/stolostron/does-not-exist.git \
  --from-literal=channel=fast \
  --dry-run=client -o yaml > cluster-image-set-git-repo-cm.yaml

  2. Apply the changes. Run the following command:

    oc apply -f cluster-image-set-git-repo-cm.yaml

  3. Delete the ClusterImageSet resources on the hub cluster to clear the hub cluster image cache. Run the following command:

    oc delete clusterimagesets --all --ignore-not-found=true --wait=true --timeout=5m

single-node OpenShift cluster installation requires matching OpenShift Container Platform with infrastructure operator for Red Hat OpenShift

If you want to install a single-node OpenShift cluster with an Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform version before 4.19, your InfraEnv custom resource and your booted host must use the same OpenShift Container Platform version that you are using to install the single-node OpenShift cluster. The installation fails if the versions do not match.

Procedure

  1. Edit your InfraEnv resource before you boot a host with the Discovery ISO, and include the following content.

    apiVersion: agent-install.openshift.io/v1beta1
kind: InfraEnv
spec:
  osImageVersion: "<4.x>"

  2. Replace <4.x> with the osImageVersion that you want to install.

Additional resources

  • ACM-15319

Managed cluster fails to rejoin hub cluster after Image-Based Break/Fix server replacement

After a bare-metal server is replaced by using Image-Based Break/Fix, or the cluster reinstallation feature of the SiteConfig operator, the managed cluster might fail to rejoin the hub cluster.

This issue occurs because the hub cluster node that hosts the API VIP retains a stale neighbor cache entry that maps the managed cluster IP address to the MAC address of the previous server.

The replacement server uses the same IP address, but has a different MAC address, which causes the hub cluster to send reply packets to the wrong Layer 2 address.

The klusterlet agent on the managed cluster display logs repeated timeout errors similar to the following message:

+

dial tcp <hub-api-address>:6443: i/o timeout

The SiteConfig operator reimport process loops indefinitely because the managed cluster never becomes healthy. To work around this issue, flush the stale neighbor cache entry on the hub cluster node that hosts the API VIP. Complete the following steps:

Procedure

  1. Identify the hub cluster node that is running the API VIP.

  2. Verify that a stale neighbor cache entry exists on the hub cluster node by running the following command. Replace <spoke-ip-address> with the IP address of the managed cluster and <bridge-interface> with the network bridge interface name on the hub cluster node:

    sudo ip neigh show to <spoke-ip-address> dev <bridge-interface>

  3. Delete the stale neighbor cache entry by running the following command:

    sudo ip neigh del <spoke-ip-address> dev <bridge-interface>

  4. Verify that the managed cluster status changes to Available by running the following command. Replace <cluster-name> with the name of your managed cluster:

    oc get managedcluster <cluster-name>

Get started

Welcome to Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes

Welcome to Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes

Kubernetes provides a platform for deploying and managing containers in a standard, consistent control plane. However, as application workloads move from development to production, they often require multiple fit-for-purpose Kubernetes clusters to support DevOps pipelines.

Note: Use of this Red Hat product requires licensing and subscription agreement.

Users, such as administrators and site reliability engineers, face challenges as they work across a range of environments, including multiple data centers, private clouds, and public clouds that run Kubernetes clusters. Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes provides the tools and capabilities to address these common challenges.

Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes provides end-to-end management visibility and control to manage your Kubernetes environment. Take control of your application modernization program with management capabilities for cluster creation, application lifecycle, and provide security and compliance for all of them across hybrid cloud environments. Clusters and applications are all visible and managed from a single console, with built-in security policies. Run your operations from anywhere that Red Hat OpenShift runs, and manage any Kubernetes cluster in your fleet.

The Welcome page from the Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes console has a header that displays the Applications switcher to return to Red Hat OpenShift Container Platform and more. The tiles describe the main functions of the product and link to important console pages.

With Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes:

  • Work across a range of environments, including multiple data centers, private clouds and public clouds that run Kubernetes clusters.

  • Easily create Kubernetes clusters and offer cluster lifecycle management in a single console.

  • Enforce policies at the target clusters using Kubernetes-supported custom resource definitions.

  • Deploy and maintain day-two operations of business applications distributed across your cluster landscape.

This guide assumes that users are familiar with Kubernetes concepts and terminology.
